hook: Philipp Moritz studied at the University of Würzburg in Germany before moving to UC Berkeley for a PhD in computer science, which he completed in 2019 while working in the university's RISELab under Ion Stoica. There, alongside fellow student Robert Nishihara, he co-created Ray, a distributed execution framework designed to support reinforcement learning and other emerging AI workloads that need to scale across large clusters. He was lead co-author of the 2018 paper "Ray: A Distributed Framework for Emerging AI Applications," which introduced a unified programming model combining task-parallel and actor-based computation. In 2019 he co-founded Anyscale with Robert Nishihara and Ion Stoica to build production infrastructure around Ray, and he serves as the company's Chief Technology Officer, leading engineering for a platform now used to scale machine learning training, inference and data processing workloads.
